name: ESP32-4832S040 (Cheap Yellow Display, 4.0in, resistive touch)
summary: The big CYD: 320x480 ST7796 on a 4MB no-PSRAM ESP32, with resistive touch, microSD, an RGB LED and a speaker on board.

render.reason: MEASURED ON THIS BOARD, and the figure that matters is what is left AFTER the display takes its share. band_height is 8 here, not the 16 the 2.4in CYD uses, and the difference is purely the width of the glass: the strips cost 2 x band_height x WIDTH x 2 bytes, so 16 rows of a 480-wide panel take 30,720 where 16 rows of a 240-wide panel take 15,360. At 8 rows this panel takes the same 15,360 the 2.4in board was tuned to, and that memory goes back to the radio. THIS WAS INHERITED WRONG AND COST A DEBUG SESSION: the whole render block was copied from cyd-2432s024n without re-deriving the band height for a panel twice as wide, and the copied reason text still did its arithmetic in 240-pixel rows. Boot ended with 12,380 free and the symptom was NOT a blank screen - the panel rendered perfectly and the board joined WiFi and got a DHCP lease. What failed was the radio: ping answered, TCP accepted the connection, and then every send() returned EAGAIN after the full 6-second httpd send timeout, because WiFi could no longer allocate a dynamic TX buffer. To a browser that is an indistinguishable 'this site cannot be reached'. At 8 rows boot ends with about 27,700 free. The cost is 40 SPI transactions per frame instead of 20, which this board can afford far more easily than it can afford a web server that accepts and never answers.

display.pixel_format_reason: The ST7796 DOES have a 16-bit SPI pixel mode, which is the one real advantage it has over the ILI9488 it is otherwise pin-compatible with: two bytes per pixel on the wire instead of three. That is a third off every blit before any other tuning.
display.clock_reason: VERIFIED at 40MHz by the panel prober, which drew a readable label, clean colour bars, a smooth grey ramp and an unbroken stripe field. Higher has not been tried; 40 is where this was proven and there is no measurement yet to justify moving it.
display.byte_swap_reason: VERIFIED true, and the instrument was the BACKGROUND, not a primary. cyd-amber declares bg as 38,38,36 - a near-black warm grey - and the panel came up vivid green. Grey is the ideal probe for byte order precisely because it is invariant under a red/blue swap: R, G and B are equal, so channel order cannot move it, and anything that DOES move it must be byte order. The arithmetic is unambiguous - (38,38,36) is 0x2124, and only the byte-swapped reading 0x2421 decodes to a green (32,133,8); every channel-order reading of the unswapped value stays grey. Corroborated by the title bar, which is filled with accent (216,142,86, orange) and rendered blue - the same swapped-byte decode - and which returns to (222,141,82) once the byte order is corrected. NOTE that the prober said the opposite (no-swap + BGR) and was wrong to, exactly as its own caveat warned: it drives this panel through Arduino_GFX, which does its own byte handling, so its colour result never transferred to esp_lcd. color_order stays bgr - with the byte order corrected the observed decode is already RGB-correct, so the two faults were one fault.
display.mirror_reason: VERIFIED mirror_x true, mirror_y false, which cancels the rotation table entirely: rotation 1 supplies mx=true, my=false, and XORing this profile in yields mirror(false, false). This panel wants swap_xy with NO mirror at all - the same orientation the ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-1.47 needed, and the reason these two fields exist rather than a fifth rotation case. THE TRAP, and it cost three flashes: under swap_xy the panel MX bit drives the SCREEN Y axis and MY drives SCREEN X, so a screen that is flipped vertically is corrected by the field named for the other axis. The field names describe the PANEL. Established from two photographs rather than from description, because a 180 turn and a single mirror are easy to confuse by eye: with mirror(T,F) the setup text kept its word order and stood on its head, and with mirror(F,T) the word order reversed. Word order is the reliable signal - a mirror in screen X reverses it, a flip in screen Y does not - and reading a whole sentence beats judging which way round one letter is.
display.invert_reason: VERIFIED false. Inversion never had to be guessed at here: the three-primary test returned saturated primaries in a recognisable permutation, and an inverting panel would have returned their complements - cyan, yellow, magenta - which is not a result anyone can mistake for red, blue and green.
display.offset_reason: VERIFIED zero. A 240-wide fill reached both edges with no shear and no black column, and the row-count test placed row 0 at the top of the glass.

bluetooth_keyboard.reason: NimBLE is 19KB of heap; Bluedroid is 83KB, which is instant OOM on a board with 20KB free. Release classic-BT memory and bring BLE up BEFORE WiFi, then WiFi.setSleep(true). The K809 keyboard bonds to whichever board it paired with last.

rgb_led.absent_reason: Present on the board, wiring not yet established.

speaker.absent_reason: Present on the board (2-pin header), wiring not yet established.

bad_baud_rates.reason: arduino-cli's default for this FQBN. Dies immediately after 'Changing baud rate to 921600... Changed.' with 'Unable to verify flash chip connection'. Never wrote a byte.

Inherited from cyd-2432s024n and WRONG here - the two boards have different CH340s. This one starts writing happily and dies mid-image: 57.7% of 907,927 bytes on the measured run, with 'No more data to read from the serial port'. That failure mode is worse than an outright refusal, because it leaves a half-written app partition that will not boot and looks like a bad build.

distinguishing_notes: Do NOT confuse with wavvy-ili9488-40. That entry is a bare 4.0in panel hand-wired to a devkit - no touch, no microSD, no RGB LED, no speaker - and it drives the panel on 18/23/5, which on THIS board is the SPI header and the microSD. Flashing it here drives the SD lines and leaves the glass dark.
Separable from cyd-2432s024n by MAC, and by the glass: 4.0in against 2.4in.
identification.confirm_prompt: Is this the 4.0in board with resistive touch, a microSD slot and a speaker header?

panel_id_register.note: Not attempted. The ILI9488 boards settled that a controller ID read is not something to build on, and this panel was identified the way they were - by drawing a labelled test card under each candidate driver and looking.

gotchas.text: Do NOT reach for wavvy-ili9488-40 because the glass is also 4.0in and also 320x480. That profile is a bare panel hand-wired to a devkit and drives the panel on sck 18 / mosi 23 / cs 5 - which on THIS board is the SPI header and the microSD. Flashing it here drives the card lines and leaves the glass dark. This board is on the CYD set: 14/13/12/2/15 with the backlight on 27.

Settled: this panel needs mirror_y, not mirror_x. Reached by reading WORD ORDER on the setup screen rather than glyph shape - X reverses the order of words, Y does not - after the prober gave three contradictory readings from single flipped letters.

byte_swap is true and was settled on the THEME BACKGROUND, not on a primary: grey is invariant under a red/blue swap, so a grey that turns green indicts byte order and nothing else. The prober had said no-swap and was wrong - it drives the panel through Arduino_GFX, not esp_lcd.

VERIFIED by probing the silicon, not by inheriting a pinout. The XPT2046 sits on the DISPLAY bus - 14/13/12 - with CS 33 and PENIRQ 36; it does NOT have a bus of its own. The widely repeated CYD touch pinout 25/32/39 was tried first and returned nothing at all, so the community answer is wrong for this board even though its CS happens to match. The test was the TEMP0 channel (control byte 0x87), a single-ended read against the internal reference that returns a stable mid-scale value with nobody touching the glass: the shared-bus candidate answered 0x31C and every other candidate answered 0x000. That distinction matters because every touch-DEPENDENT register reads zero on an idle panel, which is exactly what an absent chip reads too, so a pressure or coordinate read cannot tell a wrong pin from an untouched screen and TEMP0 can.

The XPT2046 DISABLES PENIRQ whenever bit PD0 of the control byte is 1, so a driver that reads with 0xB1/0xD1/0x91 - reference off, ADC left on, which looks like the efficient choice - holds the interrupt line high no matter how hard the panel is pressed. This cost a full flash cycle here: the first probe reported IRQ high through every press and the pin was briefly written off. Read with 0xB0/0xD0/0x90 and allow the part to power down between conversions, and GPIO 36 goes low under touch with a clean 100%/0% split across 747 samples.

Calibration, measured from the four corners in a known order rather than guessed: the controller's axes are SWAPPED relative to the screen and neither is mirrored. Touch X is the screen's VERTICAL axis and rises top-to-bottom, roughly 800 at the top edge to 3400 at the bottom. Touch Y is the screen's HORIZONTAL axis and rises left-to-right, roughly 440 to 3470. So screen_x maps from raw Y and screen_y from raw X, both without inversion. Corner medians were TL(733,464) TR(872,3551) BR(3332,3394) BL(3478,411) - note that along the top edge raw X barely moves while raw Y sweeps its whole range, which is what identifies the swap.

VERIFIED by asking the card: CMD0 answered 0x01 and CMD8 echoed the 000001AA check pattern, on VSPI at sck 18 / mosi 23 / miso 19 with CS 5, mounted read-write as a 14910 MB SDHC at 20MHz. The card is on VSPI while the PANEL is on HSPI, so unlike the 2.4in CYD - where both share one host - a card read cannot stall a frame and no bus lock is needed. Note this is the same 18/23 the wavvy-ili9488-40 profile drives as a PANEL bus, which is exactly why flashing that profile here writes to the card lines and leaves the glass dark.

present:true here describes the BOARD, not the OS. The slot, the bus and the chip select are verified - a card answers CMD0 and CMD8 on VSPI 18/23/19 with CS 5 - but penguinOS cannot mount it yet: mount_one() in eos_storage_idf.c handles EOS_FS_LITTLEFS only, and the file contains no reference to sdspi, esp_vfs_fat, sdmmc_card or FATFS at all. Its own header comment says so: '/sd is in the mount table, reports itself unmounted, and answers every call with EOS_ERR_NODEV instead of hanging on a bus that has no card on it. When the pins are found this file needs a FAT mount in mount_one() and nothing else.' The pins are now found. So a card in the slot still logs '/sd fat not present' on boot, and that line is the mount table being honest about an unimplemented mount, NOT a missing or faulty card. Whoever implements it should budget the heap: this board ends boot with about 26 KB free and FATFS wants a sector buffer and card structures out of that.
